The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act through his natural guardian,
seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident dated 04- 08-2024.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 04-08-2024 at about 08-30 am., the minor petitioner and his mother were proceeding in a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-2191 as a pillion riders, of which respondent no.1 who is the father of the petitioner was the rider and the respondent no.1 was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner on Mysore - Bengaluru main road and when they reached near Sathanuru circle, Channapatna Town, Ramanagara, at that time the rider of said vehicle suddenly applied break, so as to avoid the cow suddenly passed across the road result of which the minor petitioner and his parents fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Immediately, the minor petitioner was shifted to Chennapatna Government Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to DHEE Hospitals, Kanankapura road,
Doddakallasandra, Bengaluru wherein he admitted as an inpatient from 04- 08-2024 to 08-08-2024.
So far, the parents of the petitioner have spent more than Rs.4,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental expenses.
4. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was a student.
He was studying in 2nd standard at Mount Carmel Public School, Channapatna.
Due to the injuries sustained by the petitioner, he is unable to concentrate on his studies and unable to participate in cultural, sports and other activities.
5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 the R.C. owner of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 42-EF-2191 has remained absent.
Hence he was placed ex-parte.

6. Respondent No.2 /the Insurer of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-2191 has filed written statement and contended that they have issued a bundled policy in favour of the 1st respondent in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-EF-2191 vide policy no.671401312309000000635, the OD cover was valid from 26-05-2023 to 25-05-2024 and Third party cover is valid from 26-05-2023 Raghav A vs Arun Kumar M P on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17721349/

he cannot lodge the complaint.

In the history details it is mentioned that on 04-08-2024 at 8-25 pm., the petitioner was sitting in the front along with two pavilion rider in two wheeler, by skid child fall on left side and hit his head to ground followed by bleed from ear, nose and other injuries.

It is relevant to state here that on 04-08-2024 itself the petitioner was shifted to DHEE Hospital wherein class of vehicle is clearly mentioned, so also mentioned about two other persons traveling in the said motorcycle who are none other than the mother and father of the petitioner.
It is true that petitioner has not marked the wound certificate of the respondent no.1 to say that the respondent no.1 has also sustained injuries due to the accident.
But if the charge sheet is perused, wherein the xerox copy of the wound certificate of respondent no.1 finds place.
As per the said document the respondent no.1 too has sustained injuries but it was simple in nature.
Further in the seizure mahazar at Ex.P4 there is mention about the damages caused to the offending vehicle.

Hence, from the aforesaid materials, it can be said without any hesitation that offending vehicle itself was involved in the accident and at the time of accident petitioner was riding in the motorcycle of which his father was the rider.

17. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, when petitioner was traveling in the offending vehicle and no other vehicle was involved in the accident, under such circumstances if the respondent no.1 was driving the vehicle in slow and steady manner, even if cow suddenly came across the road, the respondent no.1 could have avoided the accident by applying break and there was no necessity to apply break suddenly.

Hence, the evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documentary evidence placed on record clearly proves the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent no.1 in which the minor petitioner has not played any role.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: In a Judgment rendered in Master Mallikarujuna / Divisional Manager National Insurance company, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that "though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of children suffering from disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors, precedents and the approach of various high courts, we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc should be if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to the whole body Rs 3 lakh , Up to 60% Rs 4 lakh, up to 90% Rs 5 lakh and above 90% it should be Rs 6 lakh .

For permanent disability up to 10%
it should be Rs 1 lakh unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
In the said case the disability is to the tune of 18% and minor was in the hospital for longer period causing inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents.

Hence the minor was compensated under the head pain and suffering already under gone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock,
hardship, inconvenience and discomfort in life on account of permanent disability to the tune of Rs 3,00,000/-.

26. As disability of the petitioner on whole body is assessed as 35%, keeping in mind the observation made in the Mallikarujuna case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering already under gone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship,
inconvenience on account of permanent disability.
27.
The guardian of the Petitioner has stated that they have spent considerable amount towards conveyance and nourishment etc..
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.25,000/- under this head.
28. So far as discomfort and inconvenience and loss of earning to the parents during the period of hospitalization of the petitioner is concerned, awarded to the tune of Rs.75,000/-.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:

29. As regarding liability is concerned, the policy covered to the offending vehicle is a bundle policy.

30. It is vehemently argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation on the ground that, as on the date of accident policy was not in force and that the respondent no.2 has issued policy of insurance in favour of 1st respondent in respect of offending vehicle from 26-05- 2023 to 25-05-2028 and the OD and package policy was valid from 26-05-2023 to 25-05-2024 and Liability policy valid from 26-05-2023 to 25-05-2028 and further insured has not renewed the OD policy from 2023 and did not paid own damages premium and the alleged accident was occurred on 04-08-2024 and the said policy does not cover the risk of the pillion rider of the offending vehicle as on the date of accident.

31. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in ILR 2011 KAR 850 between The Branch Manger, The New Indian assurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Mahadev Pandurang Patil & Anr.

entities.text: Branch Manger, The New Indian assurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Mahadev Pandurang Patil & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the deceased was the occupant in a private car.
The Tribunal fastened liability on the Insurance company to pay the compensation.
The Insurance company preferred appeal.

The question raised was "whether the occupants/passengers/inmates of private vehicle do fall within the definition of word "Third Party" it was held "The statutory Insurance is confined to the death or bodily injury to any passenger of a public service vehicle caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle in public place.
Therefore, the passenger of a vehicle which is not meant for public service is not covered under Section 147.

The said passenger in the case of a two wheeler is the pillion rider and in the case of a three wheeler and four wheeler the occupants of such vehicle who are not carried in the said vehicle for hire or reward.

Therefore, the insurance policy taken in respect of a vehicle, in which they are travelling as such passengers are not treated as third parties and such an insurance do not cover the risk of such persons.
The reason in Section 147 does not require a policy to cover the risk to passengers who are not carried for hire or reward.
The statutory insurance does not cover injuries suffered by occupants of the vehicle who are not carried for hire for reward and the insurer cannot be held liable under the Act.
The occupants/passengers/inmates of a private vehicle do not fall within the definition of the word third party.

Therefore, the legal obligation arising under Section 147 of the Act cannot be extended to an injury or death of the owner of the vehicle, passengers in such private vehicle or a pillion rider in the case of a two wheeler.
Gratuitous passengers who are not carried for hire or reward in a vehicle other than a public service vehicle, cannot be construed as third parties.

FURTHER HELD, if the risk of an occupant of a car, inmate of a vehicle or passenger in a private car, is to be covered,
additional premium has to be paid.
If no additional premium is paid, their risk is not covered.

The statutory liability under Sections 146 and 147 of the Act has to be read with the terms of the insurance policy issued under Section 146 of the Act".
32.

Hence, the Insurance company which has issued own damage policy is not liable to pay the compensation.

It was observed that "The current legal position is that, Indian Motor Tariff Endorsement No.18, which is to the effect that in Act Only Policy the insured has to pay extra premium to cover the pillion rider.
No such extra premium has been paid by the owner of the offending vehicle extending the third respondent's liability to pillion rider/deceased.

33. The learned counsel in further has referred the judgment rendered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Writ Petition (S) (Civil) No. (S) 295/ 2012 wherein the Hon'ble Apex court has taken following decisions:
"(I) It shall be mandatory for all General Insurance Companies to issue a three year third party insurance cover for new cars and five year third party insurance cover for new two wheelers as a separate product or as part of a comprehensive insurance product.
IRDA should issue instructions accordingly to all General Insurance Companies.
(ii) The GIC and IRDA should ensure that the legacy insurance date is also shared with MORTH as soon as possible for its integration with Vahan data.

(iii) IRDA should ensure that all General Insurers follow its directions dated 01-01- 2018 advising them to make available the third party insurance cover to all proposers on online channels; liaise with police authorities to facilitate issue and renewal of third party insurance cover and ensure its easy availability".
34.

sentences.text: 36. Bundle policy is a comprehensive insurance that offers vehicle damage cover and third party liability coverage.
It is a combo plan.
For one year, insured get to enjoy own damage cover along with third party coverage for three years or five years.
37. Sec.129 of MV Act requires all riders of two wheeler to wear helmet authorized by Central Government Standard.
Previously pillion riders were not covered under third party liability.
But Sec.147 now includes them for compensation in case of injury or death in Road Accident.
With the rising rate of road accident, the IRDA has introduced some crucial amendment to two wheeler Insurance Regulation for pillion rider or passengers.
The IMV Act states that all two wheeler owner must have a third party liability insurance policy.
The IRDA has mandate to cover pillion riders in third party insurance policy which will cover the injuries or death to the pillion rider.

38. Hence, when admittedly motorcycle involved in the accident insured less than one year own damage cover bundled with five years liability, it can be said that it covers even the risk of pillion rider.
Hence, the respondent no.2 being the insurer of the motorcycle is liable to pay compensation.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
39. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.8,92,100/- + cost of Rs.2,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.III, IV & V.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.8,94,100/- (Rupees Eight Lakh Ninety Four Thousand One Hundred only).
A Sum of Rs.8,92,100/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent no.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

The entire compensation amount is ordered to be deposited in the name of the minor Petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank till he attains the age of majority with liberty to withdraw periodical interest for the welfare of the minor petitioner.

Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Therefore, the insurance policy taken in respect of a vehicle, in which they are travelling as such passengers are not treated as third parties and such an insurance do not cover the risk of such persons.
The reason in Section 147 does not require a policy to cover the risk to passengers who are not carried for hire or reward.
The statutory insurance does not cover injuries suffered by occupants of the vehicle who are not carried for hire for reward and the insurer cannot be held liable under the Act.
The occupants/passengers/inmates of a private vehicle do not fall within the definition of the word third party.
Therefore, the legal obligation arising under Section 147 of the Act cannot be extended to an injury or death of the owner of the vehicle, passengers in such private vehicle or a pillion rider in the case of a two wheeler.
In CMA No. 2093/2023 between Pula Shanmugam & Anr. Vs. Yugender Ravellan & Ors., (The Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Madras).
